title: Contributing to Velclaw
summary: Contribution guide for the Velclaw project: repository workflow, validation, security, pull requests, AI-assisted development, and maintainer review.

sections.heading: Welcome
body: Velclaw is an AI-native software workspace for agents, code, builds, runtime, storage, and user services. Contributions should be focused, testable, security-conscious, and compatible with the project's existing architecture.

sections.heading: Quick links
bullets: Repository: https://github.com/velclaw/velclaw
Documentation: https://docs.velclaw.ai
Source contribution guide: CONTRIBUTING.md
Agent operating contract: AGENTS.md
Security policy: SECURITY.md

sections.heading: How to contribute
bullets: Create a dedicated branch for the change.
Make the smallest coherent change that solves the stated problem.
Run the appropriate local validation before opening a pull request.
Open the pull request against main.
Wait for automated checks and maintainer review.
Merge only after branch protection and review requirements are satisfied.

sections.heading: Issue and pull-request routing
bullets: Product bug, regression, crash, or behavior defect: describe reproduction steps, expected versus actual behavior, affected version, environment, and impact.
Documentation issue: include the affected documentation path or URL, expected content, actual content, and verification evidence.
Feature or architecture change: explain the problem, proposed solution, alternatives, scope, and operational impact before implementation.
Security vulnerability: do not publish exploit details in a normal issue or pull request; follow SECURITY.md.
Small, focused fixes may go directly to a pull request when there is enough context to review them.

sections.heading: Pull-request standards
bullets: Keep one coherent change per pull request; avoid unrelated cleanup.
Describe what changed, why it changed, and how it was validated.
Use the repository pull-request template.
For UI changes, describe affected surfaces and include before/after screenshots when useful.
Do not introduce secrets, API keys, credentials, or private data.
Keep generated documentation and source-of-truth changes synchronized when both are affected.
Do not submit refactor-only changes unless they are required for an active fix or explicitly requested.

sections.heading: Source dependencies and package management
body: The Velclaw repository uses pnpm 10.15.1. Dependencies should be declared by the package that imports them rather than relying on accidental hoisting.

examples.code:
pnpm install
pnpm format
pnpm format:check
pnpm type-check
pnpm lint
pnpm test
pnpm build

sections.heading: Before you open a PR
bullets: Run pnpm format for changed TypeScript and TSX files.
Run pnpm format:check to verify formatting.
Run pnpm type-check and resolve all type errors.
Run pnpm lint and resolve lint errors.
Run pnpm test when the change affects tested behavior.
Run pnpm build to verify the production build when application behavior or build configuration changes.
Check that no sensitive information is exposed through logs, errors, client configuration, or generated artifacts.
For UI work, validate the affected desktop and mobile surfaces where applicable.

sections.heading: Security requirements
body: Velclaw treats authentication, credentials, sandboxing, execution permissions, and secret handling as security-sensitive areas.
bullets: Never log dynamic secrets, credentials, user identifiers, repository URLs, branch names, or other sensitive runtime values.
Use generic user-facing error messages when detailed diagnostics could expose internal context.
Keep server-side diagnostics separate from user-facing logs.
Never expose private environment variables through client bundles.
Follow SECURITY.md for vulnerability reporting instead of publishing exploit details in a normal pull request.

sections.heading: AI-assisted contributions
body: AI-assisted development is supported. AI-generated changes are subject to the same engineering, security, testing, and review requirements as manually written changes.
bullets: Understand the code and behavior you are changing before submitting it.
Review generated diffs for unintended behavior, secrets, dependency changes, and architectural regressions.
Run the same validation required for equivalent human-authored work.
Keep the pull request focused and provide useful evidence for reviewers.
Use AGENTS.md as the repository operating contract for coding-agent work.

sections.heading: Documentation architecture
body: Velclaw documentation follows a layered model so each source has a clear responsibility.
bullets: Git repositories are the source of truth.
AGENTS.md defines the compact operating contract for coding agents.
OpenWiki provides source-grounded repository context and retrieval.
Docus provides human-facing platform and operational documentation.
TypeDoc provides generated TypeScript API reference.
MCP Apps documents UI integrations for MCP-enabled hosts.

sections.heading: UI and design changes
bullets: Do not replace an approved Velclaw interface without documenting the scope and reason.
Prefer the project's existing UI component patterns and design system.
Check responsive behavior for mobile when a UI surface changes.
Keep visual changes separate from unrelated refactors.
For substantial design work, compare the implementation against the approved design before requesting review.

sections.heading: Maintainer review
bullets: CODEOWNERS defines the default ownership for repository changes.
Maintainers review correctness, security, scope, architecture, and validation evidence.
Do not assume a reviewer or maintainer should be tagged unless the owned path or responsibility is directly relevant.
Address review feedback in the pull request so the durable record remains complete.

examples.code:
# install
pnpm install

# quality
pnpm format
pnpm format:check
pnpm type-check
pnpm lint

# tests and production validation
pnpm test
pnpm build

# runtime / ecosystem checks
pnpm validate:runtime
pnpm audit:ecosystem
pnpm audit:ecosystem:live

sections.heading: Contribution checklist
bullets: [ ] The change has a clear problem statement and scope.
[ ] No secrets or sensitive runtime data were introduced.
[ ] Formatting, type-checking, linting, and relevant tests pass.
[ ] Production build was checked when applicable.
[ ] UI changes were checked responsively when applicable.
[ ] Documentation was updated when behavior or developer workflow changed.
[ ] The pull request explains validation evidence and known limitations.
[ ] The change is focused and does not contain unrelated refactoring.
